belief: Any verse is a promise I can claim for whatever I want.
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that any verse is a promise you can claim for whatever you want, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: Teaching that encourages “claiming” verses for health, wealth, or success. Popular verses on posters taken out of context. Desperation for a specific outcome. Disappointment when a “claimed” promise did not come true. Misunderstanding the difference between promises and principles.
teaches: God’s promises are true, and we can trust them. But not every verse is a promise for every situation, and God’s promises are not tools for getting whatever we want. Jeremiah 29:11 was spoken to exiles in Babylon who would wait seventy years. James says we sometimes do not receive because we ask with wrong motives. We pray according to God’s will. Rightly understood, His promises give hope, but they serve His purposes, not ours.
self_statements: God promised this, so He has to do it.
I’m claiming this verse for my situation.
If it didn’t happen, I didn’t claim it right.
Every verse is a promise to me.
Philippians 4:13 means I can do anything I want.
God owes me what the verse says.
errors: Applying a promise without knowing who it was for.
Believing that “claiming” a verse forces an outcome.
Using Scripture to get what you want rather than to know God.
Concluding God failed when a misapplied promise didn’t happen.
questions: Who was Jeremiah 29:11 first spoken to, and how long did they wait?
Is this verse a promise, a principle, or a description?
What does James 4:3 say about wrong motives?
Am I asking according to God’s will or mine?
What did Paul mean by “I can do all things” in Philippians 4?
Has God failed me, or did I misunderstand the verse?
What promises of God am I sure apply to me in Christ?
truth: Not every verse is a promise I can claim for whatever I want. God’s promises are true, but I need to understand them in context and pray according to His will. His promises serve His purposes and give me hope, even in hard seasons. I can trust what He has truly promised in Christ.
hw_questions: Is this a promise, principle, or description?
What does James say about wrong motives?
Am I asking for God’s will or mine?
What did Paul mean by “all things”?
What promises in Christ are sure for me?
hw_truths: God’s promises are true when rightly understood.
I pray according to God’s will.
God’s promises serve His purposes, not my wishes.
I can read promises in their context.
God’s plans for His people include hope, even through waiting.
I can be content in Christ in every situation.

prayer: Father, thank You that Your promises are true. Help me reject the idea that any verse is a promise I can claim for whatever I want. Teach me to understand Your Word in context, to pray according to Your will, and to trust You through every season. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
